- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% for the following 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.30) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- Model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; smooth out abrupt changes in forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating positive/negative cycles, model may misalign with mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15-day moving average of past 18 days.
